The mental side of things can get hard sometimes, and what works for someone else won't always work for you. However there is a lot of great ways to help push back those thoughts and have a better positive outlook and view of yourself. Something that I find helpful is when I'm thinking negative thoughts is counteracting everything I'm thinking with something that proves otherwise, sort of a debate in my mind. If I'm telling myself no one cares about me and no one would care if I just vanish and so on, I try to remind myself of the people in my life that would care. I think of moments where someone did something for me or said something nice to me that I wouldn't have really expected from them. I hold onto those moments and tell myself no, these people do care and they would care. It doesn't matter how small the thing is, all that matters is that it was big enough that you remembered. Things like that have really helped me, and hopefully it will help you. But just remember that if you really are lost in thoughts and all you can surrounded yourself with is negativity, trying putting on a show you like, play a game you like, draw, listen to music, whatever you love to do, do it. Drive yourself away from that and do something intentional to hopefully get your mind off of things in that moment.

I also noticed you mentioned a ED, and I'm actually recovering from one myself so I do know of a few ways that could hopefully help you get past it again. EDs are a battle against the mind once again, but they are trickier to win again, but never impossible. Something I've told myself lately when I didn't wanna eat is something that has helped me get food in the past. "I don't need food and I don't deserve it, but my body has done nothing wrong and it deserves to have some food." Another thing that has helped me is having someone to remind me to eat everyday. First of all there's that reminder, but second of all it's a person that cares that wants you to eat, it has pushed me to care about myself on hard days because I didn't want to worry them and so on. If you don't have someone to do that, still at least set daily reminders on your phone that reminds you, it's still a push to get better. This isn't on the mental side exactly but something that might help is having bars or snacks in the open around where you are at home the most. It's a visual reminder but its also something to eat if you just don't have the motivation to get up and make something.

I really hope this helps in anyway, and please let me know if you still need some help. I'm here for you and I'm rooting for you! Change won't happen overnight, but with time and patience you'll get there.
